title: Freya and the Verdict
premise: Estate lawyer Lena Nakamura is hired to execute the will of Marguerite Voss, a woman whose death certificate was filed three years ago. When a stranger's body surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Lena's own closet, police treat Lena as either target or suspect, and the only person who can explain everything is the will's named witness: Freya Lindqvist, whom every record insists died in 2019. As Lena follows Freya's trail through a coastal town built on a falsified inheritance scheme, they uncover that Marguerite faked her own death to escape her family and that Freya has been hiding in plain sight as the courthouse archivist. In the end, Lena must choose between turning Freya over to close the case cleanly or destroying their spotless professional record to protect her; they choose Freya, exposing the Voss family's crimes instead and finding, for the first time, a life worth being visible in.
about_author: Ines Galloway is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent a decade watching families tear themselves apart over paper. They write mysteries about people who mistake silence for safety.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Lena Nakamura, meticulous and professionally invisible, receives a probate file for Marguerite Voss—dead on paper since 2019—demanding execution within thirty days. The document is flawless, notarized, impossible. Lena's POV establishes pride in never losing a case and a private dread of being noticed. Emotional beat: cold curiosity masking unease.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Police call Lena to identify a drowned man found wearing a jacket from Lena's own closet, down to the monogrammed cufflinks. Detective Okafor treats Lena as witness, suspect, or bait. Lena recognizes nothing about the man but everything about the staging. POV alternates briefly to the detective. Beat: the safe walls crack.

chapters.title: Thirty Days
chapters.summary: Lena begins executing the will despite warnings: the estate passes to an unnamed beneficiary unless the witness, Freya Lindqvist, appears to authenticate it. Records show Freya died four years ago. Lena visits the Voss mansion and meets the hostile surviving family. Beat: the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Family That Mourns Twice
chapters.summary: The Voss heirs—brothers Edmund and Silas, matriarch Camille—are furious the will resurfaced. Their grief feels rehearsed; their lawyer threatens disbarment. Lena notices one portrait removed from the wall, its outline still visible. Beat: everyone lies beautifully.

chapters.title: Dead Women Keep No Files
chapters.summary: Digging into Freya Lindqvist, Lena finds a birth certificate, a nursing license, then nothing after 2019—the same year Marguerite 'died.' A librarian mentions a quiet woman who volunteers at the county archive. Hope flickers. Beat: first thread pulled.

chapters.title: The Archivist
chapters.summary: In the courthouse basement, Lena meets a gray-cardiganed archivist named Wren who knows too much about probate law and flinches at the name Freya. Lena doesn't press—but leaves a business card inside a returned file. Beat: recognition without confession.

chapters.title: Second Body, Same Closet
chapters.summary: A second corpse appears, again dressed in Lena's clothing, this time in Lena's car. Okafor can no longer protect them; Internal Affairs opens a file. Someone is building a case against Lena out of stolen fabric and dead strangers. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Left Me
chapters.summary: Following the will's odd codicil, Lena finds a storage unit containing letters between Marguerite and Freya—decades of correspondence revealing deep love and a plan to expose the Voss fortune as built on a forged 1970s deed. Beat: the case becomes personal.

chapters.title: Wren After Dark
chapters.summary: Wren appears at Lena's door at midnight, soaked and terrified: she is Freya, alive because Marguerite helped her disappear when the family discovered what she knew. She refuses to authenticate the will—it would sign her death warrant. Beat: confession, and refusal.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Freya recounts 2019: how she witnessed the forgery, how Marguerite staged her own death to draw the family's attention away, how they agreed never to meet again. Lena realizes the bodies are messages meant to flush Freya out. Beat: love against duty takes shape.

chapters.title: Okafor's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Detective Okafor confronts Lena with evidence pointing squarely at them: access, motive, the clothes. Lena gambles and shares the codicil, making Okafor a reluctant ally with a deadline before IA arrests them both. Beat: trust as risk.

chapters.title: Edmund's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund Voss offers Lena a fortune to declare the will invalid and forget Freya exists. He mentions Lena's childhood group home by name—a threat dressed as empathy. Lena declines, understanding for the first time what invisibility has cost them. Beat: temptation refused.

chapters.title: The Third Message
chapters.summary: The killer strikes closer: Lena's office is ransacked, the original will stolen, and Wren's archive desk left smeared with blood that isn't hers. Freya has vanished. Lena spirals into guilt—they brought the danger to her. Beat: despair.

chapters.title: Camille's Confession
chapters.summary: Dying matriarch Camille summons Lena and admits the forgery but claims she wasn't the one sending bodies—that someone in the family is cleaning house before the truth surfaces. She gives Lena a key to Marguerite's old boathouse. Beat: the enemy has enemies.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: In the boathouse, Lena finds Marguerite alive—old, sharp, hiding exactly where no one would look—and learns the will was her final weapon: it forces the family to produce Freya or forfeit everything. Marguerite believes Freya is already dead. Beat: devastating misdirection.

chapters.title: Silas's Ledger
chapters.summary: Okafor traces the murders to Silas Voss, who has been eliminating witnesses to the forgery for years—including, he believes, Freya. The stolen clothes were bought from Lena's dry cleaner; the frame job is his insurance policy. Beat: the trap named.

chapters.title: Where Dead Women Go
chapters.summary: Lena deduces Freya's hiding pattern from the old letters' postmarks and finds her convalescing with the librarian from Chapter 5. Freya wants to run; Lena asks her, for once, to be seen. Beat: the choice crystallizes—love against duty.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Lena convenes the will reading, stalling IA with Okafor's help. Freya walks in alive, authenticates the document, and names the forged deed publicly. Silas, cornered, reaches for a gun hidden in his coat. Beat: courage on display.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Climax: Silas is subdued as Okafor arrives with the ledger evidence; Edmund crumbles and confesses to the cover-up. Marguerite emerges from hiding to face her family one last time. The price of survival comes due for everyone but Freya. Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Probate of the Heart
chapters.summary: Aftermath: Lena faces the bar inquiry but survives with a suspended censure and a reputation they no longer want to hide behind. Marguerite, formally resurrected, signs the estate over to fund the archive where Freya worked. Beat: cost accounted, peace tentative.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Lena and Freya share a quiet morning—coffee, unmonogrammed cuffs, no aliases. Lena reflects that staying invisible kept them alive but never let them live. Found family forms around them: Okafor, the librarian, even a chastened Marguerite. Beat: tenderness earned.

chapters.title: Freya and the Verdict
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Lena closes a new, ordinary will with steady hands while Freya catalogs records downstairs. A letter arrives from a stranger claiming another impossible estate—Lena smiles, and this time opens the door instead of locking it. Beat: the cycle continues, changed.
